_note: Curation, as DATA. Everything here is the part of the kit that is a judgement
rather than a measurement: which pose serves which kind of shot, which room
angle carries which kind of beat, and which plates are held back. Geometry
never appears here: that comes off the engine, which drew it.
WHAT A PLATE IS FOR IS DESIGN'S, AND IT IS NOT IN THIS FILE. Since rebuild-12
every plate carries a purpose, a caution, the chapter types it serves and, for
the sector rounds, the GICS sector its structure presumes, in the delivery's own
roles.fragment.json. The ingest reads that file and this one together: the
fragment says what each plate is for and where it belongs, this file says who
stands where and what is held back. So a new drop brings its own plate notes
and nothing here has to be retyped to keep up with it.
Written for rebuild-21 ('Bot reconstruction kit 3', 2026-09-23). Every name
below is in that kit; nothing is carried over from the drawn kit before it.
Which poses serve which kind of shot. The twelve poses are figure.js's, each
with a still, a talk strip (closed, mid and wide mouths on the head offsets),
an idle strip and a blink strip.
THE CLOSE-UP IS A WINDOW, NOT A POSE. The rebuild drew no close-up: design's
crop review (ANSWERS.md §4) found that a window on to-camera reads at
delivered scale, so scripts/kit_engine.js draws host/close-up through that
window, with all four strips. It is the only framing, and so the only member
of the roles a room with no floor falls back to. There is no medium and no
glance any more: a two-shot is a figure in a room, and he looks where his
pose looks.
checking-a-figure is the EYELINE pose and design says it needs lateral room,
so it is in panel only. sitting-at-desk is drawn in the same standing box as
every other pose (DESIGN.md §2.5), so it scales like them; it is capped at one
a video because design has not reviewed it at 1:1.

host/to-camera.purpose: square to camera, weight even: the plain talking stance

host/leaning-on-desk.purpose: talking to camera, weight on one arm

host/hands-in-pockets.purpose: listening, or between arguments. Neutral, low energy

host/holding-a-page.purpose: reading a figure out, when the page is the source of the number on screen

host/pointing-down-at-desk.purpose: the number is on the desk: pairs with a table or chart in the lower half

host/arms-crossed.purpose: the assertion: him committed to a point

host/considering.purpose: the beat between two sentences, weight settled. Not for a point being made

host/checking-a-figure.purpose: the eyeline pose: near arm raised toward the graphic side. Only where there is lateral room

host/turn-to-screen.purpose: turned to the monitor: he is reading something off it

host/head-in-hands.purpose: the cost of being right. Weary, not comic: never for a mild loss

host/walking-out-of-frame.purpose: the exit. Last host frame of a section, never mid-argument

host/sitting-at-desk.purpose: seated at his own desk: changes the scene inside a long chapter. Not yet reviewed at 1:1 by design, so once a video

host/close-up.purpose: head and shoulders, down the lens: the confession, the turn, and the line a chapter rests on. Never held on the still strip

_note: Which room angle carries which kind of beat, picked by seed within a role.
ALL FOURTEEN ROOMS ARE IN USE. rebuild-20 painted a wall item over him in four
rooms and stood him behind the monitor in the two new talk angles, so six were
held back; rebuild-21 marks every room shape as behind or in front of him and
moved the anchors, and with every pose composited in every room none of his
head is covered and at most 6% of him above the desk is (checked 2026-09-23).
So the roles are design's again: talk is the three desk angles plus the
window, read is desk-side, read-close and turn-to-screen, and panel leads with
panel-left, the angle drawn to leave the right of the frame clear for a plate.
The ingest still measures every room in a role and refuses one whose front
layer covers his head.
opener IS THE ONE ROOM A CHAPTER OPENS IN. A chapter opener is a room with the
chapter's title set in its `title` slot, and only desk-wide publishes one; the
read and talk angles are too tight to fit a card above him. The ingest refuses
an opener that publishes no title slot.
board and desk-top-down declare no host anchor, so nobody stands in them: a
beat that asks for a host there is told in the close-up. board is the index
card wall and carries the receipts role; it publishes no card slots, so the
wall of calls is not written on it.
Plates and rooms the kit ships that no shot may reach yet, each with the
reason. A held-back plate is off every chapter's menu, so the writer is never
offered it and a [PLATE] tag naming it is refused; a held-back room is in no
role. Each entry is a stem and covers both aspects.
EMPTY SINCE rebuild-21. The six legacy plates design's geometry probe flagged
(the waterfalls, insider-flow, macro-series, cycle-frame, said-happened-6)
had their slots moved clear of each other and of the safe margin, and the six
rooms that painted over him were fixed. A plate or room goes back in here with
its reason the day a drop breaks it.
WHICH HOURS AN EPISODE MAY BE SHOT AT, picked from uniformly, one per video.
The kit draws every plate at night and at dusk; this list is how often each
is used, which is a separate decision from what is drawn.
IT SAYS ["night"], DELIBERATELY, as the kit before this one did: nobody has
watched a dusk episode cut end to end. The route is to force one, watch it,
then move to ["night", "night", "night", "dusk"]. It is one line. Until
then gates.reachable_plates reports every dusk plate as unreachable, which
is the report being right. Night is first because it is the empty suffix and
what an episode with no identity to draw from gets.
The sixteen generic types, fixed. The director returns one of these plus a
display title; the type decides which plates the chapter may use and the
title is the only thing that reaches the screen.
`purpose` is ours and is what the director reads. WHICH PLATES a type may
use comes off the delivery: every plate in roles.fragment.json names its
chapter types, and the ingest files it under each. `plates` here is only
what a type adds on top of that, and `_universal` is what every type gets.

_universal._why: the set, the host, marks, row highlights and framed foreign media belong to every chapter

cold-open.purpose: the hook — the move, and why the next thirty minutes exist

how-we-got-here.purpose: the history that makes the present readable

how-the-money-is-made.purpose: the mechanism — what the business actually sells and to whom

the-numbers.purpose: the series, shown so it can be checked

one-framework.purpose: teach one idea the rest of the video leans on

moat.purpose: what stops someone else doing this

sector-comps.purpose: it did not move alone — the same moment across several names

management.purpose: who is running it, and what they have said

guidance-estimates.purpose: what they promised against what the street expects

short-interest.purpose: who is betting against it, and how crowded that is

valuation.purpose: what the price implies, and what it used to imply
valuation._why: design files the multiples strip under the-numbers only and the multiple bridge under management and bull-vs-bear; the valuation beat sets the subject against its peers' multiples and walks the trailing multiple to the forward one, so ours adds both here too

filing-walk.purpose: the document itself, read on screen

bull-vs-bear.purpose: two readings that are both true

resigned-close.purpose: the sign-off — what he is left holding

_note: The rebuild draws one outfit, so there is nothing to pick: figure.js paints
him in the kit's own cloth roles in every frame. The block stays because the
registry refuses a curation without one, and an absent block and a single
outfit are different statements.
